AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: The prognostic value of cardiac troponin elevation in atrial fibrillation (AF) is unclear.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To investigate the association of cardiac troponin elevation with adverse outcomes in AF by conducting a meta-analysis.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: We systematically searched the PubMed and Embase databases until April 2017 for studies assessing the association of cardiac troponin-T (cTnT) or troponin-I (cTnI) elevation with adverse outcomes in AF. The outcome measures were all-cause mortality and major adverse cardiac events (MACEs: death, stroke, myocardial infarction, pulmonary embolism, major bleeding, or revascularization).

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Six studies involving 22,697 AF patients were identified. Meta-analysis showed that AF with elevated cardiac troponin was independently associated with increased risk of all-cause mortality (HR 2.04; 95% CI 1.56-2.67) and MACEs (HR 1.93; 95% CI 1.61-2.30). Furthermore, the prognostic value of cardiac troponin elevation was consistently found irrespective of method determination, type of troponin measured, sample size, and study quality subgroup.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: AF with cardiac troponin elevation was independently associated with increased risk of all-cause mortality and MACEs. Therefore, determination of troponin should be considered for risk stratification in AF.
